reports.title: KRAFT HEINZ REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS;

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: For fiscal year 2026, the Company is updating its outlook. The Company now expects:
•Organic Net Sales(1)(2) down 0.5 percent to down 1.25 percent versus the prior year. This outlook includes an approximate 100 basis point impact from incremental SNAP headwinds.

•Constant Currency Adjusted Operating Income(1)(2) down 16 percent to down 18 percent versus the prior year. This outlook contemplates Adjusted Gross Profit Margin(1)(2) that is now expected to be at the low end of the previously provided range of down 10 basis points to down 50 basis points versus the prior year, incremental investments of approximately $700 million compared to 2025, and an approximate 500 basis point headwind from lapping lower incentive compensation.

•Adjusted EPS(1)(2) is now expected to be in the range of $2.07 to $2.13. Additionally, the Company expects an effective tax rate on Adjusted EPS of approximately 23.5%, interest expense of approximately $890 million, and other expense/(income) of approximately $210 million of income for the full year.
•Free Cash Flow Conversion(1)(2) of approximately 110 percent.

Current Outlook | Prior Outlook
Organic Net Sales | (1.25)% to (0.5)% | (2)% to (0.5)%
Constant Currency Adjusted Operating Income | (18)% to (16)% | (18)% to (16)%
Adjusted Gross Profit Margin | Low End of (50)bps to (10)bps | (50)bps to (10)bps
Adjusted EPS | $2.07 to $2.13 | $2.03 to $2.09

desk.headline: Sales down 2% to $6.1bn; adjusted EPS $0.53 beat; 2026 EPS outlook raised to $2.07-2.13
results: Net sales fell 2% to $6.1bn; organic sales slipped 1.1% as volumes dropped in North America (meats, sauces, drinks) and stock pulled into Q2 cost about 0.8 pts.
Emerging Markets was the bright spot with organic growth of 15.6%; North America fell 3.2% and Europe & Pacific 1.3% on an organic basis.
Adjusted operating income fell 15% to $939m on higher procurement and logistics costs, bigger bonuses and more advertising; adjusted gross margin eased to 31.9%.
Adjusted EPS was $0.53 (down from $0.61) against a $0.43 estimate, helped partly by lower interest and tax; GAAP EPS was $0.46.
Nine-month free cash flow was $2.4bn; $1.4bn went to dividends, no buybacks under the programme, and long-term debt fell to $17.1bn from $19.3bn in December.

guidance.summary: Kraft Heinz lifted its 2026 adjusted EPS range to $2.07-2.13 (was $2.03-2.09), mostly on a lower tax rate, and raised the bottom of its organic sales range to -1.25% (was -2%). Operating profit is still seen down 16-18% at constant currency, with gross margin at the low end of its range.

points: Management said US market share has levelled out, with the next push tied to retailer shelf resets in spring 2027.
Retailer destocking was worse than flagged last quarter, and US categories softened by about half a point.
Trade and marketing timing helped Q3 profit and is expected to reverse in Q4.
Cost inflation for 2027 is now seen slightly above 5%, and management said price rises will be needed next year.
Work on splitting the company remains paused; the North American coffee business is being sold with a 30% stake kept.
call.source: Call coverage: Kraft Heinz Beats On Timing And Tax While The Promised Share Turnaround Slips To 2027 — Earnings Whispers (via Finviz), 4 Nov 2026
